goal: Build a representative legal-answer benchmark that tests GitLaw beyond citation resolution: answer framing, uncertainty, retrieval completeness and reviewer correction quality.
constraints: Use public or synthetic legal questions only.
Keep legal authority with the human reviewer.
done_when: The benchmark covers representative legal-answer failure modes.
Scoring separates citation correctness from answer quality and uncertainty handling.
Baseline results identify the highest-value next regression fixes.
next_step: Build the first representative legal-answer benchmark and baseline GitLaw on it, then send the failure set to the verifier.

decision_estimate.rationale: The benchmark converts a technically strong retrieval/citation system into measurable answer-quality evidence for legal users and hiring proofs.
